conformanceSummary.story-006: CONFORMS on all 15 checklist ACs. setRoute (src/SYAHarvester.sol L157-173) computes k at the first empty pool slot, rejects any non-zero entry at path[2k+1..10] with InvalidRouteGap(i), and requires the delivered token path[2k] to equal the live rewardToken with InvalidRouteEnd(address,address). The selector is unchanged and only the param was renamed last->delivered. InvalidRouteGap is declared with NatSpec. setRoute, InvalidRouteEnd and ICurveRouterNG NatSpec all describe the first-empty-slot rule. MockCurveRouter._resolve follows the Router NG break rule, reverts NoHop/ZeroOutputToken and keeps the setRate/rate/calls/Slippage/input-pull API. Tests: registry (a) InvalidRouteGap(10) L208, (b) InvalidRouteGap(4) L234, (c) InvalidRouteGap(6) L255, 5-hop accept L278 / reject L290, no-hop non-reward InvalidRouteEnd(usdc,usde) L297, reward k=0 accept L318. Mock fidelity: gapped->path[2] L78, path[2k] L92, 5-hop->path[10] L108, no-hop revert L128. Harvest-level test_routeGap_* (3). Fork: gap rejected InvalidRouteGap(10), contiguous harvest leaves harvester empty, real Router NG delivers crvUSD and the mock agrees. harvest.sh KNOWN_ERRORS has InvalidRouteGap(uint256). One spec-internal conflict: the code block checks End before Gap while the checklist expects Gap for gapped paths. Execution Decision 3 disclosed it, and story-007 then wrote Gap->Token->End into the spec, so the shipped order now matches the latest story. The accept/reject set is identical under either order. No finding.
conformanceSummary.story-007: CONFORMS on all 10 checklist ACs. The InvalidRouteToken loop (1<=i<k, index 2i), then InvalidRouteEnd, then a per-hop loop: an executed row needs swap_type!=0, an unexecuted row must be all-zero (InvalidRouteSwapParams), then pools[h]==0 (InvalidRoutePools). The order is exactly ZeroAddress->Start->Gap->Token->End->(per hop: params, then pools), and it matches the spec block verbatim. All 3 errors have NatSpec. The setRoute NatSpec describes every rule. Tests: InvalidRouteToken(2) L393 and (6) L405, swap_type 0 on hop 0/1/4 L430/438/446, row at hop k InvalidRouteSwapParams(1) L454, pools[k] InvalidRoutePools(1) L470, k=0 reward route with a non-zero row/pool L514/522, accept 5-hop with 5 valid rows L530, single-hop row-0-only round-trip L546, k=0 all-zero accept L566. Order pins L421/486/495/506. Helpers _params(k)/_pools(k) are k-aware, and only fixture inputs changed (no assertion was weakened, verified by reading the diff). Mock: ZeroIntermediateToken (L159, L171) and BadSwapType(1) (L184); rows past the prefix are ignored (L199). Fork (a) the real router reverts with empty data and the mock reverts, (b) the real router reverts Error('Bad swap type') and the mock reverts, (c) InvalidRouteToken(2), (d) configure plus harvest leaves the harvester empty. harvest.sh has the three signatures. Real-router claims verified against the deployed Vyper source at reports/02/profiles/evidence/RouterNG-v1.1-0x16C6.vy (break rule, 'Bad swap type', 'Received nothing').

lawOneOverride.story-006: SAFE. The contiguity rule removes the M-01 strand class. Router NG transfers only the last executed hop's output_token = path[2k], so no accepted route can deliver a non-reward token. The exception is the k=0 reward-token route, which story-006 kept as 'harmless'. _sellYield skips the current reward token, but after an SYA setRewardToken the stored k=0 route for the OLD token becomes reachable if a strategy delivers it, and Router NG then reverts (hop 0 always executes). That is fail-loud with no strand, and it is already folded into L-03 by code-scan. The story's premise about that case is wrong (F-06), but the outcome is not unsafe.
lawOneOverride.story-007: SAFE. Every new rule only rejects routes. Zeroing unexecuted rows and pools costs nothing because Router NG never reads them, and swap_type 0 is never valid. All shipped MainnetRoutes pass (fork test d). The rule set is deliberately incomplete: swap_type>8, i/j, pool_type, n_coins and executed-hop pools are explicitly out of scope. The residuals fail loudly (CODE-02-001 swap_type>=9 -> 'Bad swap type'; wrong i/j -> 'Received nothing'), so no stranding is possible. The story Goal sentence ('stores only routes whose path, swap params and pools are mutually consistent with how Router NG will execute them') claims more than the spec block delivers. Recorded as a cross-reference to CODE-02-001, not a separate F, so it is not double-counted.

findings.actualBehavior: Shipped setRoute implements the story-006/007 contiguity rule. Graded literally against story-001, the code now fails story-001's acceptance (story-001 would accept a gapped route that 006 rejects), and its test intent ('last non-zero entry equals reward') is gone. story-001 has not been touched since run-01 (mtime 2026-10-24) and still names the vault CurveAMMAdapter, which still carries the M-01 bug, as the template. Story-006 calls amending story-001 'mitigation 3', and no story for it exists anywhere in the tree.
findings.deviation: The implementation follows the newest stories, and the later story explicitly says it supersedes the rule, so this is NOT an implementation deviation. Under 'later story governs' the code is conformant. A story-level conformance gap remains all the same. (1) The authoritative story tree contains two contradictory specs for setRoute, and supersession is recorded only in a Concerns bullet of 006, not on 001. (2) Story-006 frames the 001 amendment as a deferred mitigation, not as 'not needed'. (3) story-001 still points readers and agents at a vulnerable template. Anyone re-deriving or re-implementing from story-001, including a future agent grading against it or re-scaffolding a sibling harvester, would re-introduce M-01. Supersession is enough to grade the code. It is not enough to close the spec, because the stale rule is still the first thing a reader of 001 is told to copy.

findings.subtype: story premise factually wrong at k=0; NatSpec and test comments inherit it
findings.function: InvalidRouteEnd NatSpec (L81-83); ICurveRouterNG header NatSpec (L16-17); registry test comment L298; mock test comment L129
findings.specText: story-006 Background L20: "So with first empty pool slot at `path[2k+1]` (k in 0..4), delivered token = `path[2k]`"; Implementation Notes L100: "`token == rewardToken` with `path[1] == 0` (k=0, delivered = path[0] = reward) is accepted by mitigation 1."
findings.actualBehavior: Deployed Router NG v1.1 (reports/02/profiles/evidence/RouterNG-v1.1-0x16C6.vy, exchange loop) always executes hop 0 and only tests `i == 4 or _route[i*2+3] == empty` AFTER the swap. With path[1]==0 it calls address(0) as the pool and output token and reverts with empty data. It never 'delivers path[0]'. The code's InvalidRouteEnd @dev ('delivers path[2k] at the first empty pool slot'), the interface NatSpec ('delivers _route[2k] for the first k with _route[2k+1] == 0'), the registry comment ('Router NG executes nothing; the delivered token is path[0] itself') and the mock test comment ('the real router would execute nothing') all repeat the premise. The setRoute NatSpec itself is correct ('never executed').
findings.deviation: The code meets the story's behavioural AC (k=0 non-reward -> InvalidRouteEnd(reward, token); k=0 reward accepted). The story's model of the router is false at k=0, and the docs copy it. The accept/reject set is unaffected because the k=0 path is either rejected or never executed. The one reachable consequence (an old reward token after setRewardToken) fails loudly and is already under L-03.
findings.recommendation: State that hop 0 always executes, so a k=0 route is non-executable (the router reverts), and fix the two test comments. Optionally have the mock model the real revert instead of NoHop (Q-06 residual).

findings.subtype: story premise factually wrong; interface NatSpec inherits it
findings.specText: story-007 Background L273: "swap using `_swap_params[i]` (and `_pools[i]` only for zap swap types 3/5/7)"; Concerns L380: "leave executed-hop pools unconstrained because zap swap types legitimately use them."
findings.actualBehavior: In deployed Router NG v1.1, `pool = _pools[i]` is consumed only in the swap_type == 3 branch (LendingBasePoolMetaZap.exchange_underlying / CryptoMetaZap.exchange). The router's own NatSpec says '_pools ... only needed for swap_type = 3'. ICurveRouterNG L22 says '(only for the zap swap types 3/5/7)'. The SYAHarvester L98 wording ('zap swap types use them') is loose but not false.
findings.deviation: The interface NatSpec faithfully copies a wrong story premise. Behaviour is unaffected: executed-hop pools stay unconstrained, which is still correct for type 3, and a stray pool on a type-1/2 hop is simply ignored. The wrong text would mislead a future validator that ties pools to swap_type (for example, requiring pools[h]!=0 for type 5/7 would reject nothing real but encode a false model).
findings.recommendation: Change '3/5/7' to 'swap_type 3 only' in ICurveRouterNG.sol and in story-007's Background, if the owner amends stories.
